name: Harim
overview: Harim was a male figure known primarily for his descendants who returned to Judah following the Babylonian captivity, as recorded in Ezra 2:32. Although his tribal affiliation is not specified, he is mentioned in the context of the post-exilic community. Harim’s name also appears on the sealed document listed in Nehemiah 10:27, indicating his involvement or recognition among the covenant signatories.
namesAndTitles: The name Harim means 'consecrated [to YHWH],' reflecting a dedication or separation for the Lord, though it was not a name given directly by God. This proper name suggests a person set apart in some way for divine purposes, consistent with his descendants’ return to Judah.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Harim as a descendant of Jacob and traces his ancestry through several generations including Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon, Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah. Additionally, Adna is identified as his father, providing a clear lineage that situates him within the post-exilic community.
scriptureSignificance: Harim’s significance lies in his role as a patriarch whose descendants were part of the restoration of Judah after the exile, marking him as a link in the chain of God’s faithfulness to His covenant people. His inclusion on the sealed covenant document in Nehemiah highlights his or his family’s commitment to the renewed covenant community. Through his lineage, the biblical narrative preserves the continuity of God’s people during a pivotal period of return and rebuilding.
